blind_codes.Task_Type: T4 (prognostic biomarker association via Cox hazard ratios; outcome dementia-or-death; T2 arguable)
blind_codes.Sample_N: 131 MCI with baseline plasma (Cox models: 120 all-MCI, 62 probable MCI-LB, 43 MCI-AD); 161 completed baseline assessment

Task_Type.reason: Two readings. T2: the study is explicitly about MCI conversion (baseline plasma markers vs later conversion to dementia or death; results headed 'Prediction of Conversion to Dementia or Death'). T4: it reports prognostic-biomarker associations (hazard ratios, regression on annualised cognitive change) with no classifier or discrimination figure, the outcome is a composite dementia-or-death endpoint, and the key subgroup (MCI-LB) converts mainly to DLB rather than AD. My blind code was T4.
Task_Type.quote: Cox proportional hazards models were used to calculate hazard ratios for conversion to dementia or death with correction for age, sex, years in education, and MMSE.

Category.reason: Plasma Abeta42/40, GFAP, NfL and pTau181 (Simoa). ACE-R/MMSE outcome measures are a secondary C5 domain.

Validation_Type.reason: Association models only; no predictive model validated (V2 by convention).

Sample_N_Approx.reason: Every figure is in the paper and the registry says which is which: 161 completed baseline assessment (p. 3), plasma measured in 131 (p. 1), 72/131 converted or died (p. 3), Cox tables n=120 all-MCI, 62 probable MCI-LB, 43 MCI-AD (p. 3). Under the rule, an enrolled N labelled as such is a match.

Publication_Year.reason: Published online 29 March 2025; Movement Disorders Vol. 40, No. 6, 2025.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Newcastle MCI cohort recruited 2013-2019; ADNI not used.
